text:
ashley: Heads up — experiments team wants a temporary way to turn schema REJECTs into WARNs for a subset of routes so we don't break product tests while we iterate on the new tool adapters.

sam: Hmm. You mean change enforcement from hard reject to soft warning at the router level?

ashley: Exactly. We call it a 'suppressor' policy in the proposal. idea is: route-level flag + sampled telemetry + console surface. Not for prod-wide defaults.

maria: I'm worried about silent quality regressions. If we downgrade to WARN, will customers still get charged for the token/exec?

jordan: Billing question is big. My take: still bill (we used GPU/time), but mark the request as 'schema.warn' so it can be filtered out in cost reports.

sam: +1 for a tagged event. Also we should make WARNs opt-in in canary via rollout config, e.g., 1% -> 5% -> 25%.

ashley: proposed config (very rough):
```json
{
  "invoke_policy": {
    "schema_enforcement": "warn",
    "route_selector": "/experiments/ai-assistant/*",
    "sampling_pct": 10,
    "emit_event": "schema.warn"
  }
}
```

maria: If sampling_pct=10, are we only sending telemetry for 10% or only downgrading 10%? need clarity.

jordan: How about semantics: sampling_pct controls telemetry sampling (how many WARN events we capture at full detail). Downgrade applies to all matched requests. That way you can see per-route impact while minimizing storage.

sam: That makes sense technically but ops needs counters for total WARN rate (not just sampled). We can emit an aggregate metric (schema.warn.count) for every request and a separate sampled payload for traces.

ashley: good point. add both: aggregate counter + sampled traces. Also add an alert when warn.rate jumps >5% of successful calls in 5m window.

maria: Dashboard UX — the console needs a new panel: 'Schema warn vs rejects' with route filter and sample viewer so SEs can click into a sampled request. Also show model & adapter version.

jordan: We should also expose whether the request was routed to fallback variant e.g., model-compact. That impacts whether warn was introduced by adapter or model decode.

sam: ops-bot: can we get a quick spike in ingestion cost estimates for adding sampled traces?

ops-bot: ingest-estimate-bot: added estimate job (id 2026-03-insert) — expected +0.6% storage, +1.2% backend CPU for 10k warn traces / day.

maria: We need an internal opt-out: if a customer has SLA saying "no soft accepts", suppressor can't apply. auth check at router.

ashley: yeah must check org policy before downgrading. patch idea: router checks route flags and org-level enforcement flag. if org.enforce_strict == true -> always reject.

sam: Implementation details: where to do the downgrade? options:
- pre-routing (fast path)
- post-serve (after model produced response, less intrusive)
I prefer post-serve because we can tag the exact validator that failed.

jordan: post-serve also lets us include the exact decoded output in sampled traces. downside: slightly wasted compute if models are expensive. but it's acceptable for small canary.

maria: Rollout plan proposal:
1) internal canary routes only (experiments team) at 100% but org-policy enforced -> still apply for internal org only
2) public canary: 1% of traffic for selected route selector
3) add dashboard + alerts -> 5% -> 25% -> enable wider

ashley: action items:
- sam: add counter metric schema.warn.count + schema.reject.count and event tag schema.variant (warn|reject) (ETA EOD)
- jordan: console mockup for warn/reject panel (ETA Tue)
- maria: write org-policy validation and test matrix (ETA Wed)
- ashley: update router patch to post-serve downgrade + sampled-trace hook (PR draft)

sam: also add a note to billing team: tagging doesn't mean exempt from charges. ops will decide on reporting buckets.

maria: one more: make sure the CLI/SDK surfaces a warning header so SDK users can opt-in to suppressor behavior client-side for devs. header e.g., `X-Redwood-Schema-Mode: warn`

ashley: nice. I'll draft the design doc and attach with the PR. want to avoid any 'silent' experiments without visibility.

jordan: TL;DR — suppressor policy OK for short-term canary if we have: org opt-out, aggregate metrics, sampled traces, billing tag, dashboard + alert.

sam: :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Router patch branch 'suppressor-policy' created, CI kicked off.

ashley: ping me when CI green, i'll shepherd the doc + canary checklist.

maria: thanks everyone — this should help the experiments team ship without causing surprise outages.

ashley: end
